_notes: The BOOTSTRAP for the fleet config store, and nothing else reads it (docs/RUNBOOK.md, 'Where the config lives').
The live config is the store on the data volume: seed it from this file ONCE (bun runner/src/config-store.ts seed infra/fleet.example.json),
then edit it on the viewer's /config page or with the config-store CLI. The active config is operational state, never committed to git.
This file is a small, valid, representative roster that gives a fresh deployment a working board; it is not the fleet.
Fleet config 0.5. One concept, the JOB; one axis for evidence, the TIER; one axis for idle work, IDLE. Re-read every 60s.
roster.<name>.tier — how much evidence this model gets. THE only thing that sets a run count.
t0 trial     e90 x1, promotion HELD — it can never climb out on its own.
t1 standard  e90 x3, promotes to t2 on one counted e90 that reached level 5.
t2 long      e90 x3 + e360 x1.
Required on EVERY entry: the roster is a model CATALOG, so there is no
unscheduled entry left to make an exception for. objective and wikiCoords are REFUSED here —
steering is a campaign, which names the entry in an assignment and owns its own task shape.
There is no per-entry override and no per-billing table: a bespoke volume is a NAMED tier in
runner/src/models.ts, reviewed like an episode id, never a number edited into one entry.
A t0 model that earns rung 1 KEEPS the witness (--status shows `t0*`): move it to t1 and it
promotes immediately on evidence it already has, with nothing re-run. Moving a model by hand is
always allowed and never records a promotion — `promoted` is only ever said of a climb.
roster.<name>.idle — what it does with an account once its tier is spent. Absent = none.
none        nothing. What a paid model wants, and the default so idle work is never bought by omission.
unlimited   one freeplay session at a time, unscored, with no episode wall-clock cap.
It remains one continuous character/session and ends only when its 20m idle watchdog fires.
roster.<name>.routing — which backend behind OpenRouter may serve this entry (docs/RUNBOOK.md).
A name, a list in preference order, or { order, sort, allowFallbacks, requireParameters }.
ABSENT = the model author's own provider, fallbacks OFF (operator decision 2026-09-16): a
third-party provider is a deliberate, named datapoint, never a silent fallback.
REFUSED on a claude-code/codex entry or a non-OpenRouter apiBase (Cerebras, LM Studio,
OpenCode Zen): one machine behind the endpoint, nothing to route between. policy.routing sets
the fleet default; an entry's own routing replaces it whole and is never merged with it.
billing — free or paid, derived (free slug / LAN / subscription CLI -> free; else paid); roster.<name>.billing overrides.
It buys a model no runs and costs it none. To the scheduler it says only which credential may carry a run: on a metered
provider a free credential carries only free models and a paid one only paid models. Trial a paid model by giving it t0.
An openai entry's override is recorded on its runs: the ladders' "exclude free" reads it, and a recorded free needs no price.
credentials: { <id>: { provider, secretEnv, slots, budget?, billing, enabled } }, in preference order (runner/src/credentials.ts).
The one answer to "can this run start, and on what": a run takes a slot on the FIRST enabled credential that serves its
model's provider and has room under its slots and its budget, and it records that credential. No credential, no run.
provider    claude (a Claude subscription), chatgpt (a Codex home), openrouter, opencode (Zen), opencode-go, cerebras,
deepseek, local (the self-hosted server). A model's provider is its CLI driver's, or its apiBase's host.
secretEnv   the NAME of the env var holding the secret (for chatgpt, the var naming the Codex home), never the secret:
the provider's own name or that with a numbered suffix (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_2, OPENROUTER_KEY_2).
slots       how many runs may be live on it at once.
budget      absent = none. { kind: usage, scoredMaxPct?, freeplayMaxPct? } (default 80/80; claude, chatgpt, opencode-go):
a scored start holds at the scored share of a usage window, a freeplay run pauses and does not start at
the freeplay share; a spent window holds everything until it resets. { kind: spend, usdPerDay }
(openrouter: the provider's reported charge since 00:00 UTC) and { kind: runs, perDay } hold new starts only.
billing     free or paid; see billing above.
The examples below are DISABLED: a seeded store schedules nothing until the operator enables a credential.
accounts: { pool: [...], max? }. Every game account a run that names none is drawn from, one live session each, in
preference order; max caps how many are live at once (default: all). Never PROBE, never SMOKE*, never the gate's.
A DISABLED pinned job may park on a pool account; an ENABLED one may not — THAT JOB is refused and left
disabled, named in --status and the fleet log, and the rest of the config stays in effect. Same for a
pinned campaign, and for two enabled pins on one account (the first in order keeps it). A LIVE run under a
refused pin is left alone — it finishes and does not respawn. Shape errors still take the whole config down.
roster entries: NO character name. The model names its own at createSession and the run records
what it chose; `character` is REFUSED by name here, like the other retired keys — a name in the
config is one the harness must keep valid and unique, and an invalid one takes the config down.
`race`/`class` are fixed dimensions and stay.
policy: only where runs execute. maxSessions { <driver>: n } is how many sessions of a driver one host carries at once,
whichever credential pays (each CLI session is a process and a sandbox). Absent = no cap beyond the credentials' slots.
routing (the fleet-wide OpenRouter default) and runPods are here too.
A roster entry, queue job or pinned campaign may pin ONE credential with credential: "<id>": its runs take that one or
wait for it, never another. Normally absent. A pin that cannot carry the entry refuses THAT ENTRY or job, by name.
campaigns: probe campaigns, the third lane (see docs/EPISODES.md). The SHAPE of a campaign — its cells, arms,
start, leash, stopping rule, resume rule and attempt cap — is a definition file runner/campaigns/<id>@<v>.json,
PUBLISHED into the store as campaign-defs/<id>@<v> by runner/src/campaign-publish.ts (written once, never by
set/patch/delete or this page); a change is a new version, never an edit. This block holds only the dynamic
half: { <id>: { version, enabled, assignments [{ model: <roster name>, runsPerCell }], account?,
accounts?, credential?, excludeUnhealthy?, concluded? } }, strict. A row naming a version nobody published
refuses THAT campaign by name.
Every run is an unscored `probing` episode, never re-armed by a harness bump. account set = PINNED (same
rules as a pinned job); absent = the policy schedules it, between the evals and the idle work, and only on
a model that owes no eval and holds no live or paused run. Completion is DERIVED per (id, version,
assignment, arm, cell) from the counted probe runs on disk. A finished campaign gets enabled:false and
KEEPS its results — see the /campaigns page. concluded: [versions] is the operator's verdict that those
versions are finished, whatever their squares hold: they launch and resume nothing.
queue: jobs { ref | [refs], episode e90|e360|freeplay, repeat n|"loop", enabled, account?, credential? }. Never probing: a probe is a campaign's cell.
account set = PINNED to it (never policy-scheduled); absent = manual pool job, outranks the policy for a pool account.
A waiting manual job reserves the pool: the policy takes no pool account while one waits.

preflight: the smoke gate the supervisor runs before spawning, and the release's deploy smokes on top (none: the regression smokes run on demand, `bun wb smoke suite`) (docs/RUNBOOK.md); its accounts may not be in the pool or on a job.
